text:
ari: FYI I'm reverting a canary config change — we saw a big p99 spike after the rollout. Canary was 10% traffic, started ~180s ago. Rolling back now.

ari: Change was: `runtime.autoprefetch = true` + `serving.microbatch_max = 16` (intended to boost throughput for long-seq workloads).
```
# diff of canary config
- serving.microbatch_max: 8
+ serving.microbatch_max: 16
- runtime.kv_prefetch: false
+ runtime.kv_prefetch: true
```

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout started: svc=runtime-canary image=runtime:v2.3.4 cfg=canary-2026-03-17-ari

grace: wtf p99 numbers?

ari: quick numbers from canary metrics stream: p50 ~ 85ms (same), p95 ~ 210ms (same), p99 jumped from ~220ms baseline -> ~520ms on canary (2.36x). Error rate unchanged. Throughput up ~12% for that pool.

liam: interesting — throughput up but tail doubled. sounds like microbatch boundary mixing short+long sequences creating KV-cache thrash + kernel fallback. Any perf traces?

ari: yes, attached sampled profiles (summary):
- many requests hitting kernel-selection path: `quantized_kernels.v1` toggling to `fallback_fp16` at runtime when microbatch sizes hit >12 because of memory fragmentation.
- KV cache eviction rate increased 3x on canary nodes (we're evicting mid-generation for some sessions).

elena: that matches: autoprefetch=true started prefetching KV pages for predicted future tokens; combined with bigger microbatches the runtime schedules more in-flight KV windows and we saturate the async prefetch queue. Prefetch queue length + retry backoff caused head-of-line blocking for some microbatches -> long tail.

santiago: can we confirm which code change enabled autoprefetch? (PR or flag name)

ari: PR is https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/PR-3842 (autoprefetch) — it's gated behind `runtime.kv_prefetch`. I flipped it on for canary config to validate throughput.

opsbot: rollback request received for release runtime:v2.3.4 canary. Initiating rollback to runtime:v2.3.3

deploy-bot: rollback start: svc=runtime-canary target=image=runtime:v2.3.3 by=ari

grace: nice call to rollback. Any quick mitigations if we want to re-run the test? e.g., limit autoprefetch concurrency or reduce microbatch_max?

liam: reduce microbatch_max back to 8 and cap prefetch queue to 4 should avoid thrash. Also add a kernel-selection safety: if prefetch queue > 2, prefer stable fp16 kernel to avoid fallbacks.

ari: agreed. Rolling back now and opening a follow-up: revert config + add safety gate.

deploy-bot: rollback success: runtime-canary now on runtime:v2.3.3 (consistent with control)

ari: canary metrics post-rollback (10m after): p99 back to ~230ms, p95 stable, throughput returned to baseline.

raj: postmortem/action items: 1) don't enable `runtime.kv_prefetch` in canary without a preflight that simulates small/long seq mixes, 2) implement a microbatch safety cap inference: if small_seq_ratio > 30% then microbatch_max <= 8, 3) expose prefetch-queue and kernel-fallback counters as top-level alertable metrics, 4) add an automated canary SLO check that blocks config flips that increase p99 by >20% during rollout.

elena: I'll take 2 + 3 (kernel/metric hooks). Will open PRs this afternoon.

ari: I'll take 4 and the addendum to canary runbook (how to test prefetch heuristics).

grace: can we also add a quick smoke trace capture (CPU+KV traces) to the canary pipeline for the next two weeks? That would make debugging faster.

santiago: ack, will add trace capture toggle to canary jobs (low overhead sampling).

ari: thanks everyone. TL;DR: autoprefetch + bigger microbatch caused KV prefetch queue contention -> kernel fallbacks & KV eviction -> p99 spike. Rolled back canary, p99 recovered. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:

raj: nice job. let's avoid optimistic perf flips without perf-sim. :+1:
